M_fixed: For primes $p\equiv1\pmod4$ let $E_p=\max_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathbb F_p}}\sum_{i<j}\left(\frac{j-i}{p}\right)\sigma_i\sigma_j$. The circulant matrix $Q=\big(\big(\frac{j-i}p\big)\big)_{i,j\in\mathbb F_p}$ is symmetric with eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt p$ (each with multiplicity $\frac{p-1}2$) and $0$, so $E_p\le\frac12p^{3/2}$. (For the Paley graph $P_p$, $\mathrm{surp}(P_p)=\mathrm{maxcut}(P_p)-\frac12|E(P_p)|\le \frac14E_p+\frac p8$.) It is known that $\limsup_p E_p/p^{3/2}=\frac12$: if $(\frac qp)=1$ for all primes $q\le y$, then $\sigma_x=\operatorname{sgn}\cos(2\pi x/p)$ has ratio $\frac12-o_y(1)$; and the same $\sigma$ gives $E_p/p^{3/2}\ge\frac4{\pi^2}\big(2-\frac{\pi^2}8\big)-o(1)\approx0.31$ for every $p$. Determine $\liminf_{p}E_p/p^{3/2}$; in particular, is it $\frac12$?
partial_result_check: Correct. Q is circulant with eigenvalues chi(a)sqrt p (Gauss sums), so E_p<=p^{3/2}/2. Square-wave ratio is (4/pi^2)sum_{m odd}chi(m)/m^2 + o(1); taking p=1 mod 8 and p=1 mod q for odd q<=y (reciprocity + Dirichlet) gives limsup=1/2. Recomputed p=53881: 0.4925. Bonus: the sum is >=2-pi^2/8 so liminf>=0.31. But the side claim '2E_p = max-cut surplus up to O(p)' is wrong: surp = -(s^2-p)/8 + E/4 (after dilating by a nonresidue), so surp<=E_p/4+p/8; equality up to O(p) needs balanced optimisers, not shown.
